introduction.text: The Aula Regia is the great hall of the Flavian Palace on Rome's Palatine Hill, completed in 92 AD. It is a key example of Roman imperial architecture and the model for medieval audience halls across Europe.

history.description: The Aula Regia of the Flavian Palace was completed in 92 AD.
The Aula Palatina in Trier was completed in 311 AD under Constantine the Great.
The Imperial Palace of Ingelheim was built around 780 AD.
Santa María del Naranco was constructed around 850 AD as an aula regia for Ramiro I of Asturias.

design.description: The aula regia follows a single‑nave plan, unlike the basilica style. It features an apse where the ruler’s throne would be, and an entrance opposite the throne. The hall’s layout influenced later Christian church architecture.
